name: Leave Entitlements
text: The Employee shall be entitled to leave as follows, subject to the applicable State Shops and Establishments Act and other applicable labour laws: (a) Earned Leave ('EL'): Eighteen (18) days per calendar year, accruing at the rate of 1.5 days per month of service; earned leave may be accumulated up to a maximum of forty-five (45) days and any excess shall lapse; (b) Sick Leave ('SL'): Twelve (12) days per calendar year for certified medical illness; sick leave shall not be accumulated and shall lapse if unused at year end; (c) Casual Leave ('CL'): Six (6) days per calendar year for personal matters; casual leave shall not be accumulated and shall lapse if unused; (d) Maternity Leave: As prescribed under the Code on Social Security, 2020, including twenty-six (26) weeks of paid maternity leave for the first two children; (e) Public Holidays: National and state public holidays as declared by the Central and applicable State Government. Leave entitlements shall be pro-rated for periods of employment less than twelve (12) months.

legal_basis.note: Right to payment of maternity benefit — twenty-six weeks

legal_basis.act: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020

legal_basis.note: Leave entitlements for shop and commercial establishment employees. State legislation, NOT repealed by the Codes.

invalid_if: Earned leave entitlement below minimum prescribed under applicable State Shops Act
Maternity leave below 26 weeks for first two children contrary to Maternity Benefit Act 1961
source: Code on Social Security, 2020; Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020; State Shops and Establishments Acts
title: Leave Policy

jurisdiction_constraints.general: Factories Act applies to factories with 10+ workers using power; Shops Acts apply to other establishments

dispute_hotspots: Maternity leave denial — employer faces criminal prosecution under MBA S.21
Leave encashment on resignation — employer refuses to encash accumulated leave
Carry-forward limits — employee challenges forfeiture of excess leave
authoring_note: LABOUR CODES, 21 NOVEMBER 2025. The four labour Codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025, repealing the 29 central labour statutes this clause previously cited. OSH s.32 governs annual leave with wages in place of the repealed Factories Act s.78. The precise accrual rate under s.32 and the rules made under it was NOT verified and the clause's existing accrual figures have deliberately been left untouched. The advocate must check the leave accrual numbers in this clause against OSH s.32 and the applicable state rules.
